heading: INT. GRAIN ELEVATOR, TOP FLOOR - NIGHT

units.text: INT. GRAIN ELEVATOR, TOP FLOOR - NIGHT
Wind moans through the slats.
Dust drifts in a column of moonlight.
Old machinery stands like sleeping animals.
HOLLIS MERCER, 50s, a farmer in a canvas jacket, climbs through the floor hatch and holds a lantern high.
RAYMOND TUCK, 30s, his nephew, follows, breathing hard.
He sets the lantern on a beam.
He wipes his hands on his pants and listens.
Uncle Hollis, I don't like it up here.
units.name: RAYMOND

units.text: It's grain, Ray. It's just grain.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Then why's it moving?
units.name: RAYMOND

units.text: Hollis looks.
The grain in the nearest bin shifts in slow ripples, as though breathing.
He steps toward it and puts out a hand.
Dust sifts around his fingers.
He pulls it back.
Raymond grabs his sleeve.
Don't.
units.name: RAYMOND

units.text: Let go.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: He shakes him off and leans over the rail.
The lantern light sweeps down into the bin.
Something pale shifts under the surface.
Oh, Lord.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: He backs away.
He bumps into the other man, who yelps and spins, and for a moment they cling to each other, each trying to see over the other's shoulder.
What is it? Hollis, what is it?
units.name: RAYMOND

units.text: It's Dale Whitby.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Dale's been gone two years.
units.name: RAYMOND

units.text: I know it.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: The grain stops moving.
The wind drops.
From the hatch below, soft and wet, comes a sound like someone clearing his throat.
Neither of them answers.
Hollis. He's behind us.
units.name: RAYMOND

units.text: He drops the lantern.
It rolls across the floor, throws wild shadows across the beams, and goes out against a post.
